stem: A client who has completed cancer treatment asks, 'Will I need routine CT scans forever to make sure the cancer does not come back?' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Follow-up testing is individualized; the plan may include physical exams, laboratory tests, imaging, or other procedures based on the cancer, treatment received, health status, and clinical findings.
options.B: Every cancer survivor needs the same lifelong CT schedule because surveillance imaging is standardized across all cancer types.
options.C: Once treatment ends, follow-up testing is unnecessary unless the client independently discovers a new mass.
options.D: Imaging replaces follow-up visits, so clinical assessment is no longer needed when routine scans are ordered.

rationale: NCI states that all cancer survivors should receive follow-up care, but the schedule and tests are individualized. Follow-up may include physical examination, bloodwork, imaging, and other tests or procedures, with frequency and content based on the cancer type, treatment received, overall health, treatment-related problems, and clinical judgment. Imaging can be useful to monitor for recurrence in appropriate situations, but routine imaging is not a universal lifelong requirement for every cancer and does not replace clinical follow-up. New or persistent symptoms between scheduled visits should also be reported rather than waiting for the next planned scan.
educational_objective: Explain that post-treatment cancer surveillance is individualized and may include imaging when clinically appropriate rather than assuming a universal routine-imaging schedule for all survivors.

correction_summary: Rebuilt the original item because it implied scheduled surveillance imaging is broadly expected after cancer treatment and is intended uniformly to detect recurrence at an earlier treatable stage. The final item reflects NCI guidance that all survivors need follow-up but the tests and frequency are individualized; imaging is one possible component rather than a universal requirement and does not replace clinical assessment.
audit_findings: Original item overgeneralized surveillance imaging across cancers despite major cancer- and treatment-specific differences in recommended follow-up.
Fresh NCI review states that follow-up schedules and tests vary by cancer type, treatment received, overall health, and clinical needs.
NCI confirms that imaging can monitor recurrence but does not support a universal lifelong CT schedule for all survivors.
The final item preserves the role of physical/clinical follow-up and symptom reporting rather than making imaging the sole surveillance strategy.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct explanation with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported universal imaging claim, or unresolved source conflict.
